sections.h2: Where is Great Falls and why is it called the Electric City?
sections.html:
Great Falls is the county seat of Cascade County in central Montana and the third most populous city in the state. The 2020 census counted 60,442 residents in 22.9 square miles, and the metro area, which covers all of Cascade County, had 84,414.

The city sits just east of the Rocky Mountains and the Missouri River runs through it. It is named for a series of five waterfalls on the river, and three of them, Black Eagle, Rainbow and the Great Falls itself, host hydroelectric dams. That is where the "Electric City" nickname comes from. Interstate 15 serves the city from the north and south, and Great Falls International Airport sits on the west side next to the Montana Air National Guard.

sections.h2: How did Great Falls get started?
sections.html:
Great Falls was planned as an industrial city. Paris Gibson visited the falls in 1880, saw the potential for cheap hydropower, and returned in 1883 to plat a settlement on the south side of the river. James J. Hill's Great Northern Railway arrived in October 1887, and the city was incorporated on November 28, 1888.

Black Eagle Dam was completed in 1890 and was the first hydroelectric dam built in Montana. A smelter went up in nearby Black Eagle the same year. Early buildings from that era still stand, including the former Central High School, finished in 1896, and the Cascade County Courthouse of 1903. Much of the early city was built around the railroad and smelter economy, so ask your buyer how they view an older house near downtown or the river.

sections.h2: What does Malmstrom Air Force Base mean for the local housing market?
sections.html:
Malmstrom is the largest employer in the Great Falls community, and its workforce shapes demand for houses. The base reports about 3,371 active-duty members and 525 Department of the Air Force civilians, with about 3,300 family members living on or near the base. Its annual economic impact for fiscal year 2025 was approximately $444 million, and it accounted for 959 indirect jobs.

Malmstrom is one of three Air Force bases that operate the Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile, under the 341st Missile Wing. The base sits east of the city, and an estimated 6,500 veterans live in the local area.

Military assignments run on a cycle, and a family with orders can face a short window to move. A sale that depends on a buyer's loan approval can feel slow in that situation.

  • If you have orders, share your report date with any buyer or agent at the start.
  • Ask how much time a cash closing needs compared with a financed one.
  • Tell the buyer whether the house is vacant, since that can affect the closing date.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Great Falls, and what does it do to a roof and a furnace?
sections.html:
Great Falls has a cold semi-arid climate with long, often snowy winters, hot dry summers and a notable amount of summer thunderstorm rain. The wettest part of the year is spring. Chinook winds can warm the winter: afternoons above 50 degrees Fahrenheit average about fifteen across the three winter months.

The swings are large. There are on average 20.8 nights a year at 0 degrees or colder and 44 days that never rise above freezing, and highs reach 90 degrees on about nineteen days. The daily range often exceeds 30 degrees. In August 1992 a two-day snowfall totaled 8.3 inches.

A house takes this in several ways. Repeated freeze and thaw works on foundations and driveways. Roofs carry snowy winters and summer thunderstorms. Furnaces and water heaters carry long heating seasons. If you know a roof is past its age or a furnace is shaky, say so in your disclosure, because buyers will find it.

sections.h2: How does code enforcement work in Great Falls?
sections.html:
Great Falls enforces its property code mainly in response to complaints. The city describes code enforcement as complaint-driven, covering rubbish, junk vehicles and property maintenance issues. For private property, the contact is Planning and Community Development at 406-455-8574. In the public right-of-way, call Public Works at 406-771-1401.

If neighbors have complained about your yard, an open code case on the house can complicate a sale. Clear it before you list, or tell the buyer what is open. The city also has nine neighborhood councils, which are a useful place to learn what is happening on your street.

sections.h2: How are Great Falls property taxes billed?
sections.html:
Cascade County bills and collects the tax, and the schedule follows state law. Residential bills are usually mailed in late October. The first payment is due November 30, or within 30 days of the postmark if that is later, and the second is due May 31. Residential property is valued every two years at 100 percent of market value.

For the 2025 tax year, Montana changed the way it taxes homes. The rate is 0.76 percent on the first $400,000 of market value, 1.10 percent on the portion up to $1.5 million, and 2.20 percent above that, as set out on the Department of Revenue's 2025 information page. The Cascade County property tax office is at 121 4th Street North, Suite 1A, and its phone number is 406-454-6850.

At closing, any unpaid tax for the current period is normally settled through the title company. Ask for a payoff figure so you know the amount before you sign.

sections.h2: What must a seller tell the buyer in Montana?
sections.html:
A Great Falls seller has to hand over a disclosure statement covering adverse material facts the seller actually knows. Section 70-20-502 of the Montana Code lists title issues, water and wastewater systems, structural and mechanical problems, additions without a building permit, hazardous materials, drainage and soil problems, and testing for radon, mold, lead-based paint and similar items.

The statement has to be delivered before or with the contract. If it comes later, the buyer can rescind within three days under section 70-20-504. The duty is lighter for transfers ordered by a court, foreclosure sales, transfers to a spouse, child or parent, and transfers between co-owners, all of which are listed in section 70-20-503.

sections.h2: What choices do Great Falls homeowners have when they need to sell?
sections.html:
There are three realistic routes, and the best one depends on the condition of the house and on how soon you need to close.

  • A traditional listing. This puts the house in front of the most buyers. Expect showings, an inspection and a buyer with a loan, which adds time and sometimes repair requests.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale. You save the agent's commission, but you carry the marketing, negotiation and disclosure paperwork.
  • A cash sale to a company that buys houses. The buyer takes the property as it is, there is no loan to approve, and the closing date can be set around your move. The price reflects the repairs and risk the buyer takes on, so compare the written offer to your expected net from a listing.

No cash offer is guaranteed. A buyer needs to see the house and the title before putting a number on it.

sections.h2: What problems do sellers in Great Falls commonly face?
sections.html:
• A military move with a fixed report date.
  • An older house near the river or downtown with aging wiring, plumbing or a roof near the end of its life.
  • An inherited house shared by several heirs, some out of state.
  • An open code complaint over junk, rubbish or an unmaintained yard.
  • A rental with tenants or deferred repairs that the owner no longer wants to manage.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell a house in Great Falls?
faqs.a: Timing depends on the title, the buyer and how ready you are. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and loan approval, which are the steps that often slow a financed sale.

faqs.q: Do I need to fix a Great Falls house before selling it for cash?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer purchases the house as it is. You still must disclose problems you know about under Montana law.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a code complaint on my Great Falls property?
faqs.a: For private property, call Planning and Community Development at 406-455-8574. For the public right-of-way, call Public Works at 406-771-1401.

faqs.q: When are Cascade County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due November 30, or within 30 days of the postmark if that is later, and the second half is due May 31. The county property tax office can be reached at 406-454-6850.

faqs.q: Is the Malmstrom workforce a reason Great Falls homes sell quickly?
faqs.a: Malmstrom is the largest employer in the community, and the base reports about 3,300 family members on or near it. How quickly any one house sells still depends on its condition, location and price.
